terms.definition: The community of trillions of microbes, mostly bacteria, that live in and on your body.
terms.function: Helps digest food, makes vitamins, and trains the immune system.
terms.whereItIs: Mostly in the gut, and on the skin and mouth.
terms.whyItMatters: It is a huge partner ecosystem that keeps your body working and healthy.

terms.definition: The community of microbes living in the intestines.
terms.function: Helps break down food and supports digestion.
terms.whereItIs: Along the lining of the intestines.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the largest and most important part of the microbiome.

terms.definition: The many helpful bacteria in your microbiome that support your health.
terms.function: Help digest, make vitamins, and keep out harmful germs.
terms.whereItIs: Throughout the gut and on the skin.
terms.whyItMatters: They show that most microbes in you are partners, not enemies.

terms.definition: The healthy state where the community of microbes stays balanced.
terms.function: Keeps the helpful microbes in numbers stable and healthy.
terms.whereItIs: In the gut community of your body.
terms.whyItMatters: A balanced microbiome supports good health; imbalance causes problems.
